objective.value: Test whether E. coli can optimally utilize multiple alternative carbon sources via serial adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) first in L-lactate then glycerol and vice versa; elucidate the genetic and transcriptomic basis of serial adaptation; and assess serial-ALE strains for acetoin bioproduction under single and mixed-carbon conditions.
objective.notes: Abstract and Introduction final paragraph state the objective directly.

hypothesis.value: Serial (sequential single-carbon) ALE across two fitness landscapes yields a single dominant generalist lineage with universal growth advantage on both carbon sources and their mixture, avoiding the fitness trade-offs or specialist subpopulations seen in mixed-carbon ALE, and the resulting rewired physiology improves bioproduction of a value-added product (acetoin).

inference.rationale: No explicit formal hypothesis statement; inferred from 'To test whether a bacterial strain can optimally utilize multiple carbon sources' (abstract) and Discussion statement that serial ALE is expected to enable evolution of a single dominant generalist instead of co-existing sub-populations.

hypothesis.notes: Authors frame expectations but do not label a formal hypothesis.

strain.value: Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 wild-type (parental/ancestor); phase-1 evolved strains LA (lactate-adapted) and GL (glycerol-adapted); serial-ALE end-point strains LA-GL and GL-LA; LA and LA-GL derivatives with mutT and dam restored at the lacZ locus (used as acetoin production hosts); reconstructed single/sequential mutants in MG1655 background.
strain.notes: Strain list and plasmids deferred to Supplementary Table S1 (not available); lineage nomenclature LA/GL/LA-GL/GL-LA defined in Results 2.1. 'wild type' paper label corresponds to standard lab strain MG1655, not a natural isolate.

genotype.value: Adaptive mutations tracked by WGS: LA lineage - rph-pyrE 69 bp deletion (rph 619del69, E207fs; first fixed by generation 50), hfq (142 A>T), cyaA (reported as 2336 T>G in 2.2 and 2236 T>G in 2.4 - unresolved), ppsA (72 T>G), ydcI (5 A>C); GL lineage - rpoC (3610del9, V1204fs), glpK (694 G>T, G232C); second phase added ppsA (13 G>T, G5R), ydcI (686-7insG, G229fs), hdfR (463 G>T, E155*), glpK (189 A>C); mutator phenotypes of LA and LA-GL attributed to mutT and dam mutations, restored with wild-type mutT and dam at lacZ. rpoC mutant excluded from reverse engineering (essential gene difficulty).
genotype.notes: Fig. 1D table in extracted markdown has empty frequency cells; exact allele-frequency trajectories require figure rendering/supplement. cyaA nucleotide-change notation inconsistent between sections (see conflicts).

engineering_method.value: Two-phase serial adaptive laboratory evolution (serial passage at mid-exponential phase, ~800 generations per carbon source, 1400-1600 generations total); lambda-Red one-step inactivation/recombineering (Datsenko-Wanner) with pKD13 kanamycin cassette, overlap-extension PCR and pCP20 marker excision for reverse engineering of single, sequential and double mutants; restoration of mutT/dam at lacZ locus; episomal heterologous expression of Bacillus subtilis alsS and Aeromonas hydrophila alsD from plasmid pTrcHis2A-alsSD (IPTG-inducible).
engineering_method.notes: pTrcHis2A-alsSD was constructed in a previous study (Choe et al., 2022) - background element, not a design decision of this paper.

experimental_groups.value: ALE: three independent populations per lineage direction (LA->LA-GL and GL->GL-LA). Phenotyping: WT, LA, GL, LA-GL, GL-LA each in M9 glycerol, M9 lactate, and M9 mix; also acetate, D-xylose, D-glucose, LB, TB. Reverse engineering: 11 single/sequential mutants from LA-GL mutation set and 7 from GL-LA set in WT background, assayed in glycerol, lactate, and mixed conditions; double mutants glpK(694G>T)-rph-pyrE(del) and ppsA(13G>T)-rph-pyrE(del). Transcriptomics: WT and end-point strains in respective evolutionary media and mixed-carbon (10 datasets, 1205 DEGs). Biolog PM1/PM2A respiration profiling. Acetoin production: WT, GL, GL-LA carrying pTrcHis2A-alsSD in M9 glycerol, M9 lactate, M9 mix with casamino acids.
experimental_groups.notes: Methods 4.2 says 'Two independent lineages' (the two lineage directions), Results 2.1 says 'Three independent populations' were serially passaged - recorded as minor ambiguity, interpreted as 3 populations per direction.

controls.value: E. coli MG1655 wild-type as ancestral/unevolved comparator in all growth, uptake, transcriptome, cAMP, Biolog and acetoin assays; single-ALE ancestors LA and GL as comparators for serial-ALE end-point strains; negative-control wells (AUC baseline) in Biolog phenotype microarray to discriminate false-negative growth; 'control__wt_glc' sample used as baseline control for iModulon ICA against the PRECISE compendium.
controls.notes: No empty-plasmid/no-pathway negative control for acetoin production is reported in the main text.

culture_conditions.value: 30 C, oxic. ALE: 60 mL M9 minimal in 300 mL Erlenmeyer flasks, 200 rpm shaking, serial transfer twice daily at OD600 0.4-0.6 (mid-exponential), initial OD adjusted downward as growth improved. Plate-reader growth assays: 48-well, 300 uL working volume, 807 rpm double orbital, 30 C, 24 h, OD600 every 30 min. Biolog: 30 C, 48 h on OmniLog. Acetoin batch production: 60 mL, 30 C with shaking, 24 h, supernatant sampled every 2 h. Pre-cultures: 3 mL M9 with matched carbon source.
culture_conditions.notes: Cell-stock temperature printed as '80 C glycerol cell stocks' - minus sign lost in parsing; physically implies -80 C (see conflicts).

medium.value: M9 minimal medium (M9 salts, 2 mM MgSO4, 0.1 mM CaCl2) with either 0.2% (v/v) L-lactate or 0.2% (v/v) glycerol as sole carbon source; M9 mix (0.1% v/v each of glycerol and L-lactate); acetoin production media: M9 glycerol / M9 lactate / M9 mix each supplemented with 0.2% Casamino Acids and 100 ug/mL ampicillin; LB agar with 50 ug/mL kanamycin for recombineering selection; LB for pCP20 curing at 42 C; enriched LB and Terrific Broth for non-adaptive growth profiling; Biolog IF-0a GN/GP inoculating fluid with PM1/PM2A plates.
medium.notes: Only L-lactate (not D/DL mixtures) used unless stated otherwise.

dosage.value: Carbon sources: 0.2% v/v L-lactate or glycerol (single), 0.1% v/v each (mix); non-adaptive carbons: sodium acetate 0.2% v/v, D-xylose 0.2% w/v, D-glucose 0.2% w/v; kanamycin 50 ug/mL; ampicillin 100 ug/mL; IPTG 10 uM added 2 h post-inoculation; Casamino Acids 0.2%; Biolog inoculum OD600 = 0.05; cAMP assay cell input ~20 mL of OD600 = 1.0 culture.
dosage.notes: Methods 4.13 prints 'M9 lactate (0.2 v/v L-lactate)' with missing % sign (typo).

time.value: ALE: ~800 generations phase 1, then 600-800 generations phase 2 (1400-1600 total); WGS sampling every 50 generations; growth assays 24 h with OD600 at 30-min intervals; Biolog respiration 48 h; acetoin batch 24 h with supernatant sampling at 2 h intervals; IPTG induction at 2 h post-inoculation; RNASnap lysis 95 C 7 min; cAMP lysis 20 min at room temperature.
time.notes: ALE duration expressed in generations, not calendar time; per-passage wall time not reported.

replicates.value: Three independent ALE populations per lineage direction (independent_culture_replicates, biological_independence=likely); growth/fitness assays and SGR/CUR comparisons: biological triplicates (Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 captions, SD error bars); acetoin production: three biological replicates (Fig. 4 caption); Biolog PM: biological triplicates; cAMP ELISA: each sample assayed in duplicates (technical replicates); RNA-seq replicate counts not stated in main text (requires supplement).
replicates.notes: RNA-seq replicate structure and per-mutant growth-assay replicate counts not visible in main text - requires_supplement.

assay.value: Doubling time per passage from initial/final OD of serial transfers (fitness trajectory); specific growth rate (SGR) from OD600 time series; specific carbon uptake rate (CUR) by HPLC of spent media; whole-genome resequencing for mutation trajectories; reconstructed-mutant fitness assay (percent contribution = mutant SGR relative to end-point strain SGR); RNA-seq transcriptomics with PCA, DEG and iModulon/ICA analysis; intracellular cAMP ELISA (colorimetric, non-acetylation protocol); Biolog PM1/PM2A specific respiration rates (AUC); maximum acetoin specific productivity from HPLC time courses.

instruments.value: BioTek Epoch2 / Synergy HT plate readers; Shimadzu Nexera LC-40 HPLC with RID-20A RI detector and Agilent MetaCarb 87H column (0.007 N H2SO4, 0.6 mL/min, 50 C or 65 C for mixed-carbon); Covaris S220 ultrasonicator; Qubit 2.0 fluorometer; Illumina HiSeq 2500 (50-cycle SE, WGS) and HiSeq X Ten (150-cycle PE, RNA-seq); TapeStation 2200 with High Sensitivity D1000; Bio-Rad MicroPulser electroporator; Biolog OmniLog.

analysis_methods.value: CLC Genomics Workbench read trimming/mapping to NC_000913.3 (mismatch cost 2, indel cost 3, length/similarity 0.9); Quality-based Variant Detection (min coverage 10, min variant frequency 10%); mutation causality triangulation via recurrence across ALE studies and ALEdb; DESeq2 normalization and fold-change; hierarchical clustering (Euclidean, complete); PCA; OptICA/iModulon analysis against PRECISE 278-dataset compendium (100 iterations, 1e-7 tolerance, DBSCAN robust components); student's independent t-test for Biolog AUC; pairwise significance testing with P<0.05/0.01/0.001 thresholds (full matrix in Table S3).
analysis_methods.notes: Abstract calls iModulon/ICA 'machine learning analysis'. Statistical test used for SGR/CUR/productivity comparisons not specified in main text (Table S3 in supplement).

outcomes.value: Serial-ALE end-point strains (LA-GL, GL-LA) showed generalist phenotype with significantly improved SGR/CUR in both glycerol and lactate and in the mixture without trade-offs on the first carbon (e.g., GL-LA +1.89x SGR, +1.73x CUR vs GL); mixed-carbon growth advantages 1.38-2.15x over WT. Four variants (glpK, ppsA, ydcI, rph-pyrE) accounted for >80% of end-point strain fitness; glpK/ppsA specialist effects vanished in mixed carbon and were rescued/strengthened by rph-pyrE(del) (double mutants: ~2x rph-pyrE single-mutant contribution for glpK pair, >=+8% for ppsA pair). Transcriptomes diverged lineage-specifically despite fitness convergence; RpoS/GadW iModulons decreased in all evolved strains; GlpR/LldR/Zur/Crp-2 activities condition-specific. glpK-mutant strains had up to 38% lower intracellular cAMP. 82 carbons with increased respiration in >=1 evolved strain, 36 concordant across all; evolved strains grew faster on acetate/xylose/glucose but showed fitness deficits in LB/TB. Acetoin: GL-LA specific productivity highest in all conditions; ~3.7x (GL-LA) and 2.9x (GL) vs WT in glycerol; GL-LA 1.3x over GL (glycerol), 1.6x/1.4x over WT/GL in lactate; superior in mixed condition.
outcomes.notes: Exact SGR/CUR/productivity values, error bars and full statistics reside in Table S3 / Supplementary Figs (requires_supplement); mechanism of rph-pyrE epistasis stated by authors as elusive - interpretation, not validated causality.

experimental_design_object.purpose: Evolve E. coli MG1655 sequentially on two alternative carbon sources to obtain generalist end-point strains and test serial-ALE as a strain-optimization scheme.
experimental_design_object.host: E. coli K-12 MG1655 (clonal ancestral population)
experimental_design_object.intervention: Two-phase serial ALE: phase 1 ~800 generations on M9+lactate (LA) or M9+glycerol (GL); carbon switch at fitness plateau; phase 2 600-800 generations on the other carbon (LA-GL, GL-LA); 60 mL M9 in 300 mL flasks, 30 C, 200 rpm, transfer twice daily at OD600 0.4-0.6.

conditions.medium: M9 minimal + 0.2% v/v single carbon per phase
conditions.selection: fastest-growing progeny via mid-exponential serial transfer

experimental_design_object.control: Wild-type MG1655 (fitness baseline); phase-1 ancestors LA/GL as comparators for end-point strains
experimental_design_object.readout: Doubling time per passage vs cumulative generation; end-point SGR and CUR in each carbon source
experimental_design_object.analysis: Fitness trajectory plateau detection; pairwise significance vs WT (Table S3)
experimental_design_object.outcome: End-point strains LA-GL and GL-LA acquired universal growth advantage on both single and mixed carbon sources without trade-off on the first carbon; GL showed trade-off in lactate (single-ALE specialist).

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate initiation of an ALE/selection campaign; Q2: performed in this study; Q3: produced the chassis later chosen (GL-LA) for bioproduction, changing subsequent design choices.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Integrated evolution/screening campaign generating strain variants rather than targeting a pre-specified genetic change.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: E. coli K-12 exhibits suboptimal fitness on glycerol and lactate, and prior single-carbon ALE studies showed such phenotypes can be reconfigured by evolution; whether sequential adaptation across two landscapes works was seldom explored.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Outcome measured directly (growth rates, uptake rates, WGS of evolving populations).
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Choice of ALE and the 800-generation timescale explicitly built on prior studies (Ibarra 2002, Kang 2019, Sandberg 2019) rather than a newly derived mechanistic argument; sequential single-carbon design contrasted against prior mixed-carbon ALE (Sandberg 2017).
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When optimizing E. coli for utilization of multiple metabolically related alternative carbon sources (e.g., gluconeogenic glycerol and L-lactate), apply serial single-carbon ALE phases (~800 generations each to fitness plateau) instead of simultaneous mixed-carbon evolution, because sequential adaptation fixed carbon-specialist plus generalist mutations and avoided fitness trade-offs and specialist subpopulation splitting in the tested two-carbon system.
alternatives_considered: Simultaneous mixed-carbon ALE (contrasted with Sandberg et al., 2017; avoided to evade trade-offs/bet-hedging)

experimental_design_object.purpose: Identify causal adaptive mutations via whole-genome resequencing every 50 generations, using cross-study recurrence and ALEdb as causality priors.
experimental_design_object.host: Evolving populations of GL-LA and LA-GL lineages

conditions.sequencing: Illumina HiSeq 2500, 50-cycle SE, TruSeq DNA PCR-free library
conditions.variant_calling: min coverage 10, min frequency 10%, CLC Genomics Workbench

replicates.note: population-level sequencing; replicate scheme not stated in main text

experimental_design_object.outcome: Ordered acquisition of rph-pyrE(del), hfq, cyaA, ppsA, ydcI (LA) and rpoC, glpK (GL); second phase re-acquired ppsA/ydcI/rph-pyrE variants; ppsA(72T>G) and ydcI(5A>C) declined during phase 2 on glycerol.

experimental_design_object.purpose: Quantify causal contribution of each adaptive mutation by reconstructing single and sequential (temporal-order) mutants in the wild-type background.
experimental_design_object.intervention: Lambda-Red one-step inactivation (Datsenko-Wanner): overlap-extension PCR of mutant allele + pKD13 kanamycin cassette, electroporation into pKD46 cells, 50 ug/mL kanamycin selection, PCR verification, pCP20 marker excision at 42 C. 11 mutants (LA-GL set) and 7 mutants (GL-LA set); rpoC excluded (essential-gene engineering difficulty).

conditions.readout_assay: 48-well plate reader, 300 uL, 30 C, 24 h, OD600 30-min intervals

experimental_design_object.control: Wild-type MG1655; end-point strains as reference for percent-contribution calculation
experimental_design_object.readout: SGR; percent fitness contribution = mutant SGR relative to end-point strain SGR
experimental_design_object.analysis: Single vs sequential mutant comparison; generalist/specialist classification; epistasis assessment
experimental_design_object.outcome: glpK variants = glycerol specialists (~40% of GL fitness on glycerol); rph-pyrE(del) = generalist (fittest on lactate, 2nd on glycerol); hfq generalist-like but antagonistic in combination; cyaA single mutant poor on lactate; ydcI variants negligible; glpK+ppsA synergy on glycerol (+15%); four-variant combination >80% of end-point fitness.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate point-mutation introduction; Q2: constructed in this study; Q3: results identified key contributors and directly motivated the double-mutant epistasis designs.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Reverse-genetics reconstruction to resolve which evolved alleles are causal - pathway/causality dissection rather than forward pathway optimization.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: WGS revealed recurrent mutations whose individual and combined fitness effects were unknown.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Fitness of each construct directly measured in plate-reader growth assays.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: The mutations themselves originated from ALE selection, not rational design; reconstruction tested what evolution had found. rpoC exclusion was a practical constraint, not a design choice.
alternatives_considered: rpoC reconstruction (abandoned: technical difficulty of engineering essential genes)

experimental_design_object.purpose: Test whether rph-pyrE(del) rescues/strengthens specialist mutants (glpK, ppsA) under mixed-carbon conditions.
experimental_design_object.intervention: Construction of double mutants glpK(694G>T)-rph-pyrE(del) and ppsA(13G>T)-rph-pyrE(del) using the same recombineering pipeline.

media: M9 mix (0.1% v/v glycerol + 0.1% v/v L-lactate)

experimental_design_object.control: Corresponding single mutants and wild-type in identical mixed-carbon condition
experimental_design_object.readout: Percent fitness contribution in mixed-carbon condition
experimental_design_object.analysis: Epistasis: double vs single mutant fitness contribution
experimental_design_object.outcome: glpK-rph-pyrE double mutant contribution ~2x the rph-pyrE(del) single mutant; ppsA-rph-pyrE double mutant >=+8%; specialist single mutants showed near-WT contribution in mixed carbon while quadruple mutant gained +47%/+75% over rph-pyrE single and triple mutants.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: new mutant combinations constructed; Q2: this study; Q3: confirmed a genotype-level rule (generalist rph-pyrE potentiates specialists) that informs future multi-carbon chassis design.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Combinatorial genotype assembly and screening to resolve condition-specific epistasis.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Specialist mutants (glpK, ppsA) lost their fitness contribution specifically in the mixed-carbon condition whereas generalist rph-pyrE(del) retained its contribution, suggesting positive epistasis.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Direct fitness measurements of constructed double mutants.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Combination was driven by the empirical single-mutant fitness screen in mixed carbon; the proposed pyrimidine-biosynthesis/transcription-demand mechanism is explicitly stated by the authors as elusive.

experimental_design_object.purpose: Characterize global transcriptomic adaptation and condition-specific regulator activities of evolved strains.

conditions.rna_prep: RNASnap + RNase H custom rRNA depletion + DNase I

experimental_design_object.control: Wild-type in matched media; ICA baseline 'control__wt_glc'; PRECISE 278-dataset compendium
experimental_design_object.readout: Gene expression (TPM), DEGs (1205 across 10 datasets), iModulon activities
experimental_design_object.analysis: DESeq2, PCA, hierarchical clustering (Euclidean/complete), OptICA with DBSCAN
experimental_design_object.outcome: Lineage-specific transcriptome divergence despite fitness convergence; larger rewiring in phase 1 than phase 2; lldP/lldD up in lactate-evolved strains; glpK down-regulated in glpK-mutant strains; RpoS/GadW iModulons down in all evolved strains; GlpR/LldR/Zur/Crp-2 condition-specific; translation genes up in mixed carbon.

experimental_design_object.purpose: Verify that glpK missense mutations reduce intracellular cAMP (linking glycerol-3-phosphate build-up to adenylate cyclase repression).

conditions.kit: cAMP ELISA Colorimetric Kit (Cell Biolabs), non-acetylation protocol

experimental_design_object.outcome: Strains with mutant glpK derivatives had up to 38% lower intracellular cAMP than WT (Supplementary Fig. S4B).

experimental_design_object.purpose: Assess breadth of metabolic-capacity gains across diverse carbon sources (specific respiration rates).
experimental_design_object.control: Negative-control wells (AUC baseline for false-negative exclusion)
experimental_design_object.outcome: 82 carbons with significantly increased SRR in at least one evolved strain; 36 with concordant increase across all evolved strains (glycolytic intermediates, saccharides, gluconeogenic substrates).

experimental_design_object.purpose: Test whether SRR gains translate to growth gains on conventional carbons and whether trade-offs appear in rich media.

conditions.assay: same plate-reader settings as mutant growth assays

replicates.note: not stated for this dataset; Supplementary Fig. S6

experimental_design_object.outcome: Serial-ALE strains fastest on acetate/xylose/glucose; fitness deficits vs WT in LB/TB (minimal-media evolution trade-off).

experimental_design_object.purpose: Remove mutator phenotypes from LA and LA-GL before using them as bioproduction hosts.
experimental_design_object.intervention: Introduction of wild-type mutT and dam into the lacZ locus; in LA-GL, dam placed upstream of lacZ::mutT.

conditions.method: chromosomal insertion at lacZ (same recombineering toolkit context)

experimental_design_object.readout: Genotype restoration (mutation-rate measurement not reported in main text)
experimental_design_object.outcome: Restored-mutability LA and LA-GL used for acetoin bioproduction.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: targeted chromosomal edit; Q2: performed in this study; Q3: defined the final production-host backgrounds.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Host-background qualification (intent framing of a stable production chassis) rather than pathway-level flux engineering.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: LA and LA-GL carried mutT and dam mutations conferring mutator phenotypes, undesirable for stable bioproduction hosts.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Edits constructed and genotype-confirmed; mutation-rate reversion itself not quantified in main text.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper explicitly attributes the mutator phenotype to mutT (8-oxo-dGTP diphosphatase) and dam (DNA adenine methyltransferase) defects; restoring wild-type alleles acts on a well-defined DNA-repair mechanism.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When deploying ALE-derived E. coli lineages as production hosts, check and restore DNA-repair defects (e.g., mutT/dam mutator alleles) before pathway introduction, because mutator backgrounds accumulated during evolution destabilize the production genotype - validated here only for lactate/glycerol-evolved MG1655 lineages used for acetoin production.

experimental_design_object.purpose: Assess whether serial-ALE chassis improves acetoin production from single and mixed alternative carbons.
experimental_design_object.host: WT, GL, GL-LA (mutT/dam-restored backgrounds per Methods 4.6)
experimental_design_object.intervention: Transformation with pTrcHis2A-alsSD expressing B. subtilis alsS and A. hydrophila alsD; IPTG induction (10 uM, 2 h post-inoculation); production in M9 glycerol / M9 lactate / M9 mix each + 0.2% Casamino Acids + 100 ug/mL ampicillin, 30 C, 24 h batch, sampling every 2 h.
experimental_design_object.control: Plasmid-bearing WT and single-ALE GL in identical media
experimental_design_object.readout: Maximum specific acetoin productivity (HPLC); substrate uptake rates
experimental_design_object.outcome: GL-LA highest specific acetoin productivity in all conditions: ~3.7x and 2.9x vs WT in glycerol (GL-LA, GL); GL-LA 1.3x over GL in glycerol; 1.6x/1.4x over WT/GL in lactate; superior in mix; highest productivity when lactate consumption fastest.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q2 fail: the production plasmid pTrcHis2A-alsSD and the alsS/alsD expression design were constructed in a previous study (Choe et al., 2022) and merely reused here; the production test validates the ALE chassis rather than constituting a new pathway-engineering decision.

experimental_design_object.purpose: Enable acetoin production with glycerol or lactate as sole carbon substrate despite plasmid-encoded metabolic burden.
experimental_design_object.intervention: Supplementation of production media with 0.2% Casamino Acids as exogenous nitrogen/amino-acid source.

conditions.media: M9 + carbon source + 0.2% Casamino Acids + 100 ug/mL ampicillin

experimental_design_object.control: None reported for the supplementation choice itself
experimental_design_object.analysis: Comparison across strains and carbon sources
experimental_design_object.outcome: Condition enabled growth and production on glycerol/lactate as sole carbons; plasmid burden (delayed lag, low density) noted.

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1: deliberate fermentation-medium modification; Q2: this study; Q3: made sole-carbon production feasible, shaping the production-assay design.
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Fermentation/process-level condition adjustment rather than genetic change.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Plasmid-bearing strains showed delayed lag phase and low cell density (plasmid-encoded metabolic burden), and prior acetoin processes used LB or amino-acid-supplemented defined media.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Resulting growth and productivity measured directly.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Media choice explicitly benchmarked against prior acetoin production studies (Li 2010; Nielsen 2010; Tong 2016; Nakashima 2014; Novak 2020; Shen 2012) rather than a new mechanistic derivation.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When producing acetoin in E. coli minimal medium with glycerol or L-lactate as the sole carbon source under plasmid-borne alsSD expression, supplement Casamino Acids (0.2%) as exogenous nitrogen/amino-acid source, because plasmid-encoded metabolic burden limits growth and prior acetoin fermentations relied on enriched or amino-acid-supplemented media.
alternatives_considered: defined media with exogenous amino acids (both cited from prior work)
